review.translation: [And he said|0], “ [I heard|3] [the sound of you|2,1] [in the garden|4], [and I was afraid|5] [because|6] [I|8] {was} [naked|7], [so I hid|9].”

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר introduces the man’s reply. The shift to first person in אֶת קֹלְךָ שָׁמַעְתִּי (“I heard your voice”) marks the start of his quoted speech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In אֶת קֹלְךָ שָׁמַעְתִּי, “I heard your voice,” אֶת marks קֹלְךָ as the object of שָׁמַעְתִּי. The possessive suffix on קֹלְךָ makes the object definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Adam says אֶת־קֹלְךָ שָׁמַעְתִּי בַּגָּן, “I heard the sound of you in the garden.” This recalls verse 8, where the couple heard the sound of Yahweh God walking in the garden and hid.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: The ending ־תִּי marks the speaker as the subject. The direct object אֶת קֹלְךָ means “your voice,” so the speaker says he heard God’s voice in the garden.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular

analysis.evidence: In אֶת קֹלְךָ שָׁמַעְתִּי בַּגָּן, בַּגָּן gives the location where the speaker heard the addressee’s voice. The article identifies the garden already in view.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ (assimilated into גּ), followed by a common-gender singular absolute noun in pausal form.

analysis.evidence: The speaker says he heard God's voice in the garden. He gives the reason for his fear in כִּי עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי, “because I was naked,” and then describes his response with וָאֵחָבֵא, “and I hid.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, first person common singular, with prefixed conjunction וָ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי (“I am naked”) as the reason for וָאִירָא (“I was afraid”).
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי, “because I was naked,” עֵירֹם describes the speaker, identified by אָנֹכִי (“I”). He gives his unclothed state as the reason he was afraid and hid.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used predicatively, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי, “because I was naked,” עֵירֹם is the predicate and אָנֹכִי is its subject. The speaker gives his own nakedness as the reason for his fear.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, first person common singular.

draft.change: Add the Niphal sense “hide oneself” with Genesis 3:10 as defining evidence. Retain the Hithpael sense attested in Genesis 3:8.
draft.definition: In the Niphal, to hide oneself from sight.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:10 the man uses וָאֵחָבֵא, “and I hid,” to recount his own part in the hiding described in Genesis 3:8.

analysis.evidence: The man says that he heard Yahweh God in the garden and was afraid because he was naked. With וָאֵחָבֵא he tells what he did in response, taking cover among the trees as described in Genesis 3:8.
analysis.morphology: Verb, Niphal wayyiqtol, first person common singular, with prefixed conjunction וָ־.
